static_traits.name: Li Nan
static_traits.educational_background: Currently studying for a master's degree
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends and family, but recently has become more distant from friends and family due to negative thinking
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy before; no similar problems appeared in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, able to concretely describe emotional and bodily sensations (chest tightness, insomnia); high cooperativeness; 'should' phrasing and self-comparison tendencies; sensitive to external evaluation

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling inadequate and regretful in graduate school, persistently doubting my academic choices and ability, believing I should have become a crime-fiction writer; these negative feelings gradually intensified starting from the self-study period, and are especially strong when facing difficult assignments or exams.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to relieve persistent failure and regret, improving academic performance and overall health; hoping to move out of negative thinking, reduce anxiety, and enjoy artistic creation again.

core_beliefs: My value depends on others' evaluations

special_situations.event: Encountering difficult assignments or exams in graduate school
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform poorly in graduate school, it proves I am not good enough and chose the wrong path
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying time management techniques and talking with friends to reduce stress, but still repeatedly self-doubting
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have done crime-fiction writing instead of graduate school; I am not suited for academia

special_situations.event: Approaching an art exhibition and thinking about audience viewing and purchasing behavior
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If no one buys or recognizes my paintings, it shows I am unworthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Deliberately attends to the positive aspects of her work, but is soon overwhelmed by negative thoughts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No one will buy my paintings

special_situations.event: Thinking about how others will evaluate one's work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' opinions determine my sense of worth and ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Presets others' negative evaluations internally to 'guard in advance' against blows
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will find my paintings amateurish, not worth their time or money

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback from friends and colleagues
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Praise from people around me is not credible; it may just be politeness or because of our relationship
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Dismissing positive information, persisting in self-criticism to maintain 'cautious low expectations'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, saying nice things because they know me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen and recognized academically and artistically, and to confirm self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being dismissed by others and judged as 'not good enough'; fearing wrong choices leading to failure
defense_goal: Reducing the blow of external dismissal by doubting praise, maintaining low expectations and self-criticism

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a student / artist who may be dismissed at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks about others' evaluations of the work, or points out that he has received positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others' praise is insincere, just out of politeness or because they know me
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing distrust of praise in a calm but firm tone, giving the reason 'they know me so they are polite', avoiding in-depth discussion of positive feedback's credibility.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about exhibition sales and audience reactions, or facing situations with unknown outcomes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Presupposing the worst will happen, to psychologically 'prepare in advance' for failure and dismissal
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Frequently making negative predictions in a worried, conservative tone, emphasizing 'preparing mentally in advance', avoiding accepting more balanced possibilities.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about academic and career choices, a large number of 'should/must' self-demands appear
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Taking others' or society's standards as must-follow rules without digesting them
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Frequently using phrasing like 'I should / must...', in a rigid tone, emphasizing the importance of external standards, weakening personal interests and inner experience.

manifestations: Repeatedly makes self-demands in 'should' sentences, torn over the academic path and the career choice (crime-themed writing)
Taking whether the artistic creation is recognized by others as the yardstick for action, feeling that choices are constrained by outside evaluation
When doubting the academic path and artistic value, finds it hard to continuously gain a sense of meaning and satisfaction from creating
Overly ties the value of his work to others' evaluations, weakening inner sources of meaning
outcomes: Losing lasting pride in one's creations
Overall decline in sense of well-being

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Presupposing the audience will find the work 'amateurish, not worth their time and money'
Believing friends' and colleagues' positive feedback is 'insincere, just politeness'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Persistent self-doubt and harsh self-blame during creation
When facing an exhibition, over-scrutinizes oneself and lowers action confidence

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Uses others' evaluations and social standards as the core basis of self-worth

exception_events.target_problem: When preparing or creating artworks, Li Nan is usually trapped by intense Self-doubt and worry about others' evaluations, leading to anxiety and insomnia.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At certain moments of completing works, Li Nan focused on creation itself rather than others' views, experiencing genuine pride and satisfaction, with anxiety temporarily relieved.
exception_events.reason: Clue: when he shifted attention to the joy and original intention of creation, not overly pursuing external recognition, different experiences and better emotional outcomes appeared.

positive_force: Has supportive friends and family who can provide emotional support
Able to experience pride and satisfaction when focusing on the process (potential for an inner sense of meaning)
Willing to seek help and accept psychological counseling, with motivation to change
negative_force: Frequent 'should' sentence patterns lead to rigid self-demands
Excessive comparison and Self-denial, relying on external evaluation
Dismissing positive feedback, presupposing negative outcomes, increasing anxiety and withdrawal
Disturbed sleep and difficulty concentrating, further weakening functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-denial and anxiety when facing graduate school assignments/exams or art exhibitions (accompanied by chest tightness, insomnia)
antecedent: As art exhibitions and the creative process approach
target_behavior.core_reason: Over-tying self-worth to external evaluation, setting rigid standards with 'should' phrasing, while negatively predicting future outcomes
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome things (failure and being dismissed), gaining superficial safety and control through self-criticism and low expectations
target_behavior.consequence: Academic performance affected, worsened sleep disorder and difficulty concentrating, withdrawing from socializing and support

target_behavior.behavior: Dismissing or belittling when receiving others' positive feedback (questioning the sincerity of praise)
antecedent: When friends and colleagues give positive evaluations or encouragement
target_behavior.core_reason: Maintains a negative self-schema to avoid dashed expectations and further setbacks, preserving cognitive consistency
target_behavior.function: Self-protection (reducing uncertainty and disappointment brought by external evaluation), avoiding emotional fluctuations
target_behavior.consequence: Finding it hard to accumulate confidence and positive experiences, further social alienation, persistent self-doubt
